generatedCommentsNodes.comment: The `limit` field is not serialized in `writeTo` and is explicitly set to `null` when reading from `StreamInput`. This means the internal limit optimization is lost if the logical plan is ever serialized and deserialized (e.g., for caching or debugging). Furthermore, the assertion `assert limit == null` in `writeTo` will cause crashes in environments where assertions are enabled whenever an optimized plan containing a limited `MvExpand` is serialized.

The cast `(int) limitSource.fold()` assumes that the limit expression always evaluates to an integer. While limits are typically constants in ESQL, this could lead to a `ClassCastException` if the system ever allows non-constant expressions or different numeric types for limits.

review_comment: This rule seems to cover more cases than simply LIMIT->MvExpand, which the other rule now covers. Presumably the iterative application of the other rules will cover this scenario already, so this removal is of no consequence. And presumably test coverage will pick this up if that is not the case.
